title: The Offerings to Thy Throne Which Rise
description: The Offerings to Thy Throne Which Rise in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 19, “The Heart's Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Th'of-fer-ings to Thy throne which rise, Of min-gled praise and prayer, Are but a worth-less sac-ri-fice, Un-less the heart be there.

lines: The offerings to Thy throne which rise,
No tribute but the vow sincere, —
Our offerings will indeed be blest,
If Thy pure spirit touch the breast
O, may that spirit warm each heart
And to life's lowly vale impart

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
